title: observability: add token-level KV cache cost/latency dashboard + alert tuning
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: ops and SRE teams need finer-grained observability into KV cache behavior for tokenized workloads to explain cost spikes and latency regressions. This PR adds a token-level KV cache dashboard that correlates token-level cache hits/misses with per-token latency and per-token cost breakdowns, plus adjusted alert rules to reduce noisy paging while surfacing real regressions. Summary of changes: 1) new Grafana dashboard (dashboards/token-kv-cost-latency.json) with panels for: token-level cost per model, token-level avg latency, KV hit/miss ratio by prefix length, aggregation over customer tiers, and histogram of token latencies; 2) new Prometheus collector hooks to emit kv_cache_token_hit and kv_cache_token_latency_ms with labels (model, tenant_id, prefix_len_bucket); 3) alert rule tuning (alerting/token_kv_cost_latency.rules) that adds a three-stage alert (warning/critical/auto-silence) based on sustained increase in cost-per-token and drop in KV hit ratio with runbook links; 4) tracing tweaks to add token-level trace tags and span attributes for KV cache path so traces link to dashboard panels; 5) docs and runbook updates (docs/observability/kv-metrics.md) and a small CI test (+integration) to sanity-check metrics emission. Checklist: - [x] dashboard JSON (reviewed for layout and variable usage) - [x] metrics name and labels agreed with metrics guild - [x] alert thresholds reviewed with SRE (Liam) and product (Maya) - [x] e2e integration test for metric emission - [x] docs + runbook updated - [x] smoke tested on staging (observability stack) Rollout plan: apply metric collector and tracing changes with feature flag, deploy to staging for 48h, enable dashboard, monitor for false positives, then enable alerts in prod with gradual scope (10% tenants -> 100%). Why this matters: token-level signal lets us explain unit-cost variance and helps Optimize recommend quantization/batching knobs per workload. Related: follows on earlier token-level observability PRs and ties into ENG-4821 (Optimize telemetry for KV cache).

review_conversation: Ethan Brooks (reviewer): Left a few nits on label naming—prefer kv_cache_token_hit over kv_token_hit to stay consistent with existing metric prefixes. Also suggested adding tenant tier as a label for better aggregation.
Priya Shah (author): Thanks — renamed metric to kv_cache_token_hit and added tenant_tier label. Updated docs to call out cardinality risks and recommended aggregation interval.

Liam Carter (reviewer, SRE): Alert thresholds look reasonable, but suggest a transitional silencing policy to avoid pager fatigue during rollout. Please add an auto-silence for 1h when we flip on alerts for new tenants.
Priya Shah (author): Added staged alerting with auto-silence action for initial rollout. Included runbook link and a script to silence alerts via API for canary tenants.
Maya Patel (product): Confirmed dashboard panels map to product-relevant KPIs; asked to include a panel that splits cost by model variant for A/B analysis.
Priya Shah (author): Added model_variant panel and updated variable templates so teams can filter quickly. Responding to all comments and pushed new commit. Approving pending CI.
CI system: grafana-lint failed on dashboard JSON (missing panel descriptions), author fixed and re-ran; full CI passed on second run.
Ethan Brooks: Approved. Marked as ready to merge after final CI green.
release_notes: Adds a token-level KV cache observability dashboard (cost and latency), new Prometheus metrics (kv_cache_token_hit, kv_cache_token_latency_ms), tracing span tags for KV paths, and tuned alert rules with staged rollout/runbook. This enables better diagnosis of per-token cost regressions and reduces noisy alerts during rollout.
